title: Criterion-based accreditation framework
description:
A framework that defines criteria an INSTITUTION evidences, rather than outcomes a graduate attains. NAAC (Binary accreditation plus Maturity-Based Graded Levels, post-February 2025) and NIRF use this shape.

Why this is a separate schema from framework-outcomes: NAAC does not define its own outcome set. It consumes outcome evidence produced under some other framework — a programme accredited under NBA GAPC v4.0 supplies its CO/PO attainment as evidence towards NAAC criteria. Modelling NAAC as an outcome set would invent eleven NAAC outcomes that do not exist, and would make a programme appear to be accredited twice over on the same axis.

The `evidence_sources` block is what makes the consumption explicit and machine-checkable: a criterion declares which computed artefacts satisfy it.

assessment_model.description:
binary — accredited / not accredited, no grade (NAAC post-Feb-2025).
graded_levels — maturity levels, e.g. NAAC MBGL 1-5.
weighted_parameters — a weighted score, e.g. NIRF.
qualitative — narrative judgement with no numeric outcome.

This exists so a report template can refuse to render a retired shape: NAAC's CGPA/RAF grading (A++ to C) is gone, and emitting it would produce a submission in a format the body no longer accepts.

institution_scope.description: True when criteria apply to the institution as a whole rather than to a single programme. NAAC is institutional; this is why its results do not belong on a programme attainment report.

retires.description: Assessment models this version withdraws, so a template can hard-fail rather than silently produce an obsolete submission.

verified_on.description: Last date a human checked this file against the official manual at source_url. Null means nobody has yet; when null, verification_note is required and the staleness badge reads UNVERIFIED. Never fill this in to make a badge go green.

verification_note.description: Required when verified_on is null: what state the transcription is in, and what a verifier must check.

levels.description: Required when assessment_model is graded_levels — e.g. NAAC MBGL levels 1 to 5.

criteria_required.description: Criterion codes that must be satisfied to reach this level.

weight.description: Marks or points, where the body assigns them. Absent under a purely binary model.

metric_type.description: Quantitative metrics can be computed from held data; qualitative ones need a written submission and cannot be auto-filled.

evidence_sources.description: Which computed artefacts satisfy this criterion. This is the join between an outcome-based framework and a criterion-based one: it lets an evidence pack be assembled from data the attainment engine already produced, instead of being re-keyed by hand into a submission portal.

kind.description: 'external' means the criterion cannot be evidenced from attainment data at all and needs a separate submission — stating that is more useful than pretending coverage.
